facts.fact: 火车上，Ambrose 上尉的故事还没讲完就突然停住
facts.anchor: On the train, Captain Ambrose stopped short, his story not yet finished.

facts.fact: 他用「鹅走过坟墓」的俗语解释自己的异感
facts.anchor: You know the old saying, of course, about a goose walking over your grave?

facts.fact: Fell 太太催他继续讲 Halvorsen 的故事
facts.anchor: But for now – please – finish your story. About poor Mr Halvorsen.

facts.fact: 追 Halvorsen 时他们遇见的恶灵在靠近时瞬间消失
facts.anchor: as we approached, the entity vanished as swiftly and as completely as any stage illusion.

facts.fact: Halvorsen 随身带着一枚古罗马银币 denarius
facts.anchor: a tarnished silver coin from many centuries past. A Roman thing. A denarius, I believe it’s called.

facts.fact: 上尉解释有的恶灵附着于物、有的附着于人
facts.anchor: For some spirits, ma’am, they attach themselves to objects. Others attach themselves to people.

facts.fact: Scrooge 把银币抛向空中而不是河里
facts.anchor: Then Scrooge threw the coin high up into the air – straight up, not towards the water.

facts.fact: 三秒后银币凭空落回他掌心
facts.anchor: Three long seconds later and the coin fell back into it, from thin air so far as I was able to tell.

facts.fact: 一个半月后 Halvorsen 即将登船前往 Johannesburg
facts.anchor: just before he was due to board a ship that was bound for Johannesburg.

facts.fact: 火车向英格兰边缘疾驰
facts.anchor: the train roared on, moving with impatient speed towards the very edge of England.
